messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1717654321 - elevated p99 streaming latency observed across prod-eu for SSE and websocket routes. Auto-page on-call. https://redwood.internal/incidents/1717654321
alice: I'm on it. looking at dashboards — p95 ~220ms, p99 spiking to ~4.6s starting ~02:12 UTC. Lots of chunking gaps in response streams.
bob: confirmed on proxy side. spike lines up with 'slow-consumers' counter rising and many zero-byte proxy write events in logs.
carmen: checking client metrics, seeing a small subset of sessions with stalled read windows and tx backpressure. probable slow mobile clients.
dinesh: pasting proxy snippet for context:
```
proxy-01 [02:13:05] client=10.0.5.12 write_bytes=0 stalled_for=12s route=/v1/stream
proxy-03 [02:13:09] client=10.1.8.44 txbuf=65536 write_delay=8s
```
alice: that matches: server emits chunks but clients not consuming, causing buffer growth and head-of-line for other streams.
oncall-sre: plan triage steps: 1) reduce proxy write_timeout and enable soft-kill for stuck writers 2) scale streaming runtime pool +2 3) enable auto-fallback to lower-latency model variant 4) temporarily throttle top offending clients. Who can apply proxy tweaks? @bob
bob: I can canary a config change to edge nginx (shorter proxy_send/proxy_write) to two instances now.
carmen: also suggests adding an immediate metrics alert for per-connection tx_pending_bytes > 1MB for > 10s; filing follow-up after we stabilize.
dinesh: scaling now:
```
kubectl scale deploy/streaming-runtime -n prod --replicas=12
```
# executed by dinesh
alice: patching canary nginx with: proxy_send_timeout 10s; proxy_read_timeout 60s; proxy_buffer_size 8k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 16k;
bob: canary applied to 2 edges, no errors in logs so far.
support-bot: Heads up: active SSE sessions may reconnect. If customer impact increases we'll post on status page.
carmen: model routing note: control plane has fallback policy to model-small when observed tail >2s. we can enable auto-fallback to help p99.
oncall-sre: enabling streaming_auto_fallback flag now via control plane API.
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://controlplane/api/flags/enable?flag=streaming_auto_fallback
```
alice: fallback enabled.
dinesh: new pods coming up, should be ready ~30s.
oncall-sre: monitoring — immediate effect: p99 dropped from ~4.6s -> ~1.1s after fallback + scale. p95 steady ~180ms. Good but still watching.
carmen: runtime CPU hit ~85% during fallback; acceptable for now but watch for OOM.
alice: still see a handful of stuck connections. I'm going to apply temporary iptables limit for top offender IPs (10m window).
```
sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.5.12 -m limit --limit 1/min -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.5.12 -j DROP
```
oncall-sre: do not drop for longer than 10 minutes and document it in incident notes. Need to verify if this is client bug vs expected mobile behavior.
bob: request: add per-socket queue depth metric and an alert threshold. I'll create a ticket after incident for runtime instrumentation.
incident-bot: Escalation: paging window 30m. Incident assigned -> oncall-sre. Status: mitigation in progress.
dinesh: checked customer-side traces for one affected session: mobile app was backgrounded and stopped reading socket — backlog built up.
carmen: matches. action item: implement server-side keepalive probes and soft-notify-before-close to give clients chance to recover.
oncall-sre: post-mitigation actions to capture: 1) aggressive keepalive + quicker soft timeouts 2) add per-connection consumer health in Console 3) KB for customers about mobile background socket behavior
alice: I'll open PR for keepalive defaults + canary for 48h. Also implement server-sent 'slow_consumer' event before tearing connection.
bob: instrumenting per-socket tx_pending_bytes, will alert if >1MB for >10s. filing ticket ENG-RUNTIME-2134.
support-bot: Support contacted top 3 impacted customers. Customer A saw reconnects but no data loss; Customer B reported UI stuck until manual reload.
oncall-sre: current metrics: p99 ~900ms, p95 ~160ms, error rates steady. Continue monitoring for 20m, then move to postmortem.
dinesh: adding notes and logs to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1717654321/postmortem
alice: small implementation note: prefer sending a JSON event {"type":"slow_consumer"} before hard close so clients can gracefully handle it.
carmen: will implement 'soft-notify-then-close' flow in runtime.
oncall-sre: handing to infra team for 2-hour watch. If p99 >1.5s re-open page. Great job, team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigation: partial. Owner: oncall-sre. https://redwood.internal/incidents/1717654321
support-bot: Posted customer status: "Issue mitigated, monitoring. Postmortem forthcoming." :white_check_mark:
bob: switching to async follow-ups due to code freeze; will coordinate on ENG-RUNTIME-2134.
oncall-sre: final handoff notes: create follow-ups for long-term fixes: client health telemetry, graceful soft-close, backpressure-aware batching. Assign to eng-runtime + devex.
alice: acknowledged, will sync with product for KB and Console UX changes.
carmen: saved offending IPs and sample traces in incident doc.
dinesh: no OOMs, pods stable. setting 30m watch then closing paging.
oncall-sre: closing live page at 02:48 UTC, moving to retrospective/postmortem. Thanks everyone.
support-bot: Customer comms updated. Will publish postmortem in next 48h. :memo:
